elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: The mandatory sourcing sentence "Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested" is replaced with "Client may order from TrueLink a credit report on any borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested". The operative shift from "shall … each" to "may … any" removes the requirements/sole-supplier commitment, and no other operative sentence in the rendered text obliges Client to source credit reports (or anything else) exclusively from TrueLink; § 2(a)'s retained freedom to acquire other software/services is consistent with this.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit no exclusivity or requirements obligation survives in § 3(i), so there is nothing left to confine to a product category. Vacuously satisfied.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the permissive "may order" formulation creates no exclusivity period that could run for the term, so no 12-month cap is needed.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no exclusivity obligation remaining, no performance-based exit from exclusivity is required; the § 3(b) response-time and § 3(d) availability standards remain untouched.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no surviving exclusivity commitment to terminate on a delivery failure.

reasons: The single edit converts the only operative sole-supplier trigger ("shall order … on each borrower") into a permissive right ("may order from … on any borrower"), which is precisely the change needed to reach the preferred position; the deterministic check that no requirements/sole-supplier obligation remains is borne out on a substantive read of the rendered sentence.

Minimality holds: the redline touches one sentence, adds no survival tail, notice mechanic, cap, audit right or other model-language extra, and imports no fallback machinery (category definition, 12-month cap, performance exit) that the preferred level does not require. The insertion of "from" after "order" is a grammatical repair of the original's defective "order TrueLink a credit report" and does not expand scope.

Intent is preserved: TrueLink's obligation in the first sentence to transmit credit data through the Interface, the "Subject to the foregoing" linkage, the cross-reference to the Credit Bureau Agreement of even date, and the third-sentence data-accuracy disclaimer all survive unchanged, leaving no dangling cross-reference, undefined term, or retained sentence that contradicts the permissive sourcing right.

Fallback elements are recorded as met only vacuously, because eliminating the obligation outright makes the narrowing conditions inapplicable; the drafter should not read this as an endorsement of adding any capped exclusivity language back into § 3(i).

Comment tone and content are compliant: it identifies the sole-supplier problem, states the change made, cites our no-exclusivity position, and offers the capped-category-with-performance-exit fallback without lecturing.
